artboards.title: 2 · Mid-chain — the film and its scenes

annotations.text:
The four questions this redesign has to answer:

1. What is a chain, and how do I start one?
2. Which scene am I on?
3. What does rendering actually cost — does it redo everything?
4. Where is the long joined film, versus one scene?

No fork here any more: a single prompt is always continuable, because every render IS scene 1 of a chain. Asking someone to choose 'one clip' or 'a chain' up front asks them to predict, unseen, whether a prompt is worth building on — and picking wrong used to mean a wasted render.

THE MAIN FIX. Today the newest clip's card holds the cumulative film — scene 1's card is 5s, scene 2's is 10.8s — and nothing says so. Here the joined film is ONE named panel at the top with its own scene-ticked scrubber, and the scenes below are segments with their own ~15s durations. Two different things, two different places.

The resume is invisible today. Making the work ledger explicit — four scenes 'restored', one 'sampling' — is what makes the chain's whole value legible, and explains why authoring is held while the GPU is busy.
